'''Jerome (Jerry) Arthur Goldstein''' (born August 5, 1941 in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]]) is an American [[mathematician]] whose main interests are [[partial differential equations]], [[operator theory]], [[stochastic analysis]], [[fluid dynamics]], [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]], and [[mathematical finance]].

== Career ==

Goldstein earned his B.S,  M.S. and [[Ph.D.]] degrees at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 1963, 1964 and 1967. His Ph.D. thesis ''Stochastic Differential Equations and Nonlinear Semigroups'' was supervised by [[Malempati M. Rao]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|15007}}</ref>

He held appointments as [[Professor]] of Mathematics at [[Tulane University]] (1968–91), and [[Louisiana State University]] (1991–96). Since 1996 he is  Professor of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Memphis]].

In addition, he has held visiting positions at universities in Austria, Brazil, England, France, Germany, Italy, Scotland and the United States.

== Work ==

Jerry's papers and his book<ref name="Goldstein1985">{{cite book|last=Goldstein|first=Jerome A.|authorlink=Jerome Goldstein|title=Semigroups of linear operators and applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kybvAAAAMAAJ|accessdate=September 19, 2011|year=1985|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-503540-7}}</ref> on operator semigroups include fundamental contributions to his research areas. His list of publications presently includes more than 250 items.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/mathscinet/search/publications.html?pg1=IID&s1=74805 Jerry's list of publications at MathSciNet]</ref>

He is editor of more than 10 journals, including ''[[Semigroup Forum]]'',<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130204050213/http://www.springerlink.com/content/103374/|title=Semigroup Forum}}</ref> ''Differential and Integral Equations'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aftabi.com/DIE.html |title=Differential and Integral Equations |access-date=2011-07-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326200239/http://www.aftabi.com/DIE.html |archive-date=2012-03-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  ''Advances in Differential Equations'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aftabi.com/advancesindiffer.html |title=Advances in Differential Equations |access-date=2011-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711160236/http://aftabi.com/advancesindiffer.html |archive-date=2011-07-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''Positivity'',<ref>[https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/mathematics/journal/11117 Positivity]</ref> ''Journal of Evolution Equations'',<ref>[https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/mathematics/journal/28 Journal of Evolution Equations]</ref> and ''[[Mathematische Nachrichten]]''.<ref>[http://www.wiley-vch.de/publish/en/journals/alphabeticIndex/2239/ Mathematische Nachrichten]</ref>

Jerome Goldstein has advised 29 PhD-students<ref>{{MathGenealogy|15007}}</ref> and has 78 coauthors.<ref>[http://ams.math.uni-bielefeld.de/mathscinet/search/authors.html?coauth=74805 his coauthors]{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== Awards ==

In 2006 Goldstein received Willard R. Sparks Eminent Faculty Award<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.memphis.edu/provost/award_eminent.php |title=Recipients of Willard R. Sparks Eminent Faculty Award |access-date=2011-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120403071608/http://www.memphis.edu/provost/award_eminent.php |archive-date=2012-04-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> from the University of Memphis, and in 2002 he was the recipient of the Distinguished Research Award from the University of Memphis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.memphis.edu/cas/dis_res_aw.htm |title=Distinguished Research Award, University of Memphis |access-date=2011-07-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101023153131/http://www.memphis.edu/cas/dis_res_aw.htm |archive-date=2010-10-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  In 2004-2007 he held the Dunavant Professorship at the University of Memphis.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://memphis.edu/cas/rec_dunavant.htm |title=Recipients of Dunavant Professorship |access-date=2011-07-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316101540/http://memphis.edu/cas/rec_dunavant.htm |archive-date=2012-03-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During his years at Tulane University, Goldstein received the first Faculty Award for Excellence in Research (1985) given by Tulane University.

In 2013 he became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]], for "contributions to partial differential equations and its applications, and to the dissemination of mathematics to a wider public".<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], [[American Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2013-11-04.</ref>
